raw_case_text:
The 40-year-old male patient presented initially with multiple petechiae and ecchymosis on his legs, which had appeared during his summer holidays. Emergency blood count revealed pancytopenia and bone marrow biopsy proved aplasia; vSAA was diagnosed with neutrophils under 0.1/nL, platelets under 20/nL and reticulocytes 2 per mille. Immunosuppressive therapy with antithymocyte globulin (ATGAM ; Pfizer, days 1-4; 40 mg/kg, 3,400 mg daily) and cyclosporine A was initiated but did not improve the blood count. Subsequently, repeated admissions to hospital were necessary due to febrile neutropenia. Additionally, he developed pretibial erysipelas after a mosquito bite on day -66 before SCT. Despite the initiation of broad spectrum anti-infective therapy, his clinical condition deteriorated with increasing inflammation scores and fever. SM was detected in blood cultures and in drained pus gained from the pretibial ulcers (Fig. 1). In addition, computed tomography and microbiological workup of bronchoalveolar lavage revealed invasive aspergillus flavus and SM pneumonia. Based on resistogram (sensitivity towards ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole and tigecycline; despite inpatient intolerance towards trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole), the anti-infective medication was modified, but therapy proved difficult, prolonged and required repeated modification of the antibiotic regime. The wounds (6 x 4 and 2 x 2 cm) had to be surgically revised repeatedly (in detail: incision and drainage on day -54; debridement of extensors tendon sheath and of muscles, negative wound pressure therapy on day -40; debridement and renewing of negative wound pressure therapy on days -33 and -28, finally debridement of muscles and resection of extensor hallucis longus muscles' tendon on day -23 before SCT) and were initially treated with bandages changed daily and then with negative wound pressure therapy (for illustration see Fig. 1). Due to necrosis and initially exposed wound conditions, extensor hallucis longus muscles' tendon had to be resected and extensor tibialis anterior muscles' tendon atrophied resulting in a drop foot, which was treated with a peroneus orthesis. Over the following weeks and despite intensive wound management, no signs of wound healing occurred and amputation was discussed. In addition, the patient developed septic cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 32%) with symptomatic congestive heart failure. Since his complex invasive infections (necrotizing deep skin ulcers, aspergillus pneumonia) were all caused by vSAA, the patient underwent a salvage allogeneic HSCT in October 2016, 6 months after diagnosis. The conditioning regimen consisted of cyclophosphamide (day -6 to -3 at doses of 300 mg/m2, qd), fludarabine (day -6 to -3 at doses of 30 mg/m2, qd), antithymocyte globulin (Thymoglobulin ; Genzyme, day -4 to -3; 3.75 mg/kg bodyweight [bwt], qd) and total body irradiation with 2 Gy on day 0. He received 1.01 x 106 CD34+ bone marrow stem cells/kg bwt from an unrelated, male, human leukocyte antigen allele matched 10/10 donor. Prophylaxis of Graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) consisted of tacrolimus, starting on day -5, combined with methotrexate given at doses of 10 mg/m2 on day +1 and 8 mg/m2 on day +3 and +6. Engraftment of granulocytes and leukocytes occurred both on day +22 and of thrombocytes on day +33. G-CSF was administered daily from day +2 to day +17 to avoid prolonged neutropenia in the setting of very severe infectious complications. The anti-infective medication consisted of aciclovir, moxifloxacin, atovaquone, isavuconazol and amphotericin B.
Concerning the pretibial wounds, extensive surgical debridement was continued and of two 20 cm gentamycin mini chains were placed into the deep ulcers combined with debridement and renewing of negative pressure wound therapy on days +40 and +47. On day +54 after allogeneic SCT, autologous full-thickness meshed skin graft transplantation from his lower leg was performed in the absence of signs of acute GvHD (for results see Fig. 2).
Antifungal medication was continued for 1 year leaving post inflammatory residue in sectional images. Cardiomyopathy recovered and left ventricular ejection fraction improved up to 46%. On day +650 the patient is alive and doing well in complete remission of vSAA. The use of the orthesis and intensive physiotherapeutic therapy resulted in nearly unaffected mobility (almost unremarkable drop foot, compensation by discreet hyperflexion in hip joint while walking, only lateral toes can be lifted, active plantar flexion only up to 30 degrees and dorsiflexion to up 10 degrees, nearly no active inversion and reduced eversion; muscle strength 4/5).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 40-year-old male presented initially with lower extremity petechiae and ecchymoses due to very severe aplastic anemia, subsequently developing refractory febrile neutropenia, deep necrotizing pretibial ulcers after a mosquito bite, pneumonia, and symptomatic heart failure.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with very severe aplastic anemia (vSAA) after presenting with leg petechiae and ecchymoses during summer holidays, the patient failed immunosuppressive therapy with horse ATG (40 mg/kg/day x 4 days) and cyclosporine A. On day -66 prior to salvage allogeneic HSCT, a mosquito bite on his shin progressed into two deep necrotizing pretibial ulcers (6 x 4 cm and 2 x 2 cm) with Stenotrophomonas maltophilia bacteremia, invasive Aspergillus flavus and S. maltophilia pneumonia, and septic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 32%).
subjective.past_medical_history: Very severe aplastic anemia (vSAA) refractory to antithymocyte globulin and cyclosporine A; inpatient intolerance to trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for initial leg petechiae/ecchymoses, recurrent febrile neutropenia, painful necrotic pretibial ulcers with foot drop, dyspnea/cough from pneumonia, and congestive heart failure symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Initial petechiae and ecchymoses on the legs; subsequently developed two deep necrotizing pretibial ulcers (6 x 4 cm and 2 x 2 cm) with exposed necrotic extensor tendons and muscle requiring resection of the extensor hallucis longus tendon and atrophy of the tibialis anterior tendon, resulting in a drop foot (compensated with a peroneal orthosis; final muscle strength 4/5). Signs of symptomatic congestive heart failure were also present pre-SCT.
objective.routine_investigations: Baseline CBC and bone marrow biopsy confirmed vSAA (ANC <0.1/nL, platelets <20/nL, reticulocytes 0.2%). Blood cultures and pretibial wound pus cultures isolated Stenotrophomonas maltophilia (susceptible to ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, TMP/SMX, and tigecycline). Echocardiography showed septic cardiomyopathy with LVEF 32% (recovering to 46% post-SCT).
objective.advanced_workup: Thoracic CT and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) microbiological workup confirmed dual invasive pulmonary infection with Aspergillus flavus and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Very severe aplastic anemia (vSAA) complicated by invasive pulmonary Aspergillus flavus pneumonia, concurrent Stenotrophomonas maltophilia pneumonia, bacteremia, and deep necrotizing pretibial ecthyma/myonecrosis, and septic cardiomyopathy, confirmed by blood, wound, and BAL cultures and thoracic CT. Treated with salvage 10/10 HLA-matched unrelated donor allogeneic bone marrow transplantation (conditioned with cyclophosphamide, fludarabine, Thymoglobulin, and 2 Gy TBI; G-CSF days +2 to +17; neutrophil engraftment on day +22), 1 year of systemic antifungal therapy (isavuconazole and amphotericin B) plus targeted antibacterials (moxifloxacin/ciprofloxacin/tigecycline), repeated surgical wound debridements with local gentamicin chains and negative-pressure wound therapy, and autologous full-thickness meshed skin grafting on day +54. At day +650, the patient was alive in complete hematologic remission with healed leg grafts, near-normal mobility using a peroneal orthosis, and recovered cardiac function (LVEF 46%).
